notes: 20 fully solved NEET (UG) samples for approval: 5 per section, every stem style. All original.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A ball is thrown with a speed of 30 m/s at an angle of 30° above the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s², the maximum height reached by the ball is:

solution.explanation: Only the vertical component of velocity, u sin θ, decides how high the ball rises. It rises until this component becomes zero.
steps: Vertical component: u sin θ = 30 × sin 30° = 15 m/s
At the top, vertical velocity = 0, so 0 = (15)² − 2gH
solution.why_others_wrong: 45 m uses the full speed (u²/2g). 22.5 m forgets the 2 in 2g. 5.625 m divides by an extra 2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (physical quantity) with List-II (dimensional formula).

List-I:
A. Planck's constant
B. Pressure
C. Impulse
D. Surface tension

List-II:
I. [M T⁻²]
II. [M L² T⁻¹]
III. [M L⁻¹ T⁻²]
IV. [M L T⁻¹]

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Write each quantity from an equation that defines it, then replace every term by its dimensions.
steps: Planck's constant h = E/ν: [M L² T⁻²] / [T⁻¹] = [M L² T⁻¹] → II
Pressure = force/area: [M L T⁻²] / [L²] = [M L⁻¹ T⁻²] → III
Impulse = force × time: [M L T⁻²] × [T] = [M L T⁻¹] → IV
Surface tension = force/length: [M L T⁻²] / [L] = [M T⁻²] → I
solution.shortcut: Impulse has the same dimensions as momentum, [M L T⁻¹], and h has the dimensions of angular momentum, [M L² T⁻¹].
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two cells of emf 6 V and 4 V, with internal resistances 1 Ω and 2 Ω respectively, are connected in parallel (positive terminal to positive terminal). A 4 Ω resistor is connected across the combination. The current through the 4 Ω resistor is:

solution.concept: Kirchhoff's current law at a junction (cells in parallel)
solution.explanation: Let V be the common terminal voltage. The currents from the two cells add up to the current in the resistor.
steps: Current from the 6 V cell: (6 − V)/1; from the 4 V cell: (4 − V)/2; through the resistor: V/4
Multiply by 4: 24 − 4V + 8 − 2V = V, so 7V = 32 and V = 32/7 V
Current through 4 Ω = V/4 = 8/7 A ≈ 1.14 A
solution.why_others_wrong: 10/7 A treats the cells as if in series (10 V across 7 Ω). 5/4 A averages the emfs and ignores internal resistance. 1 A uses the 4 V cell alone.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A charged particle moving parallel to a uniform magnetic field continues to move in a straight line.
Reason (R): The magnetic force on a moving charged particle does no work on it.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: When v is parallel to B, v × B = 0, so there is no force and the particle is not deflected: A is true. The magnetic force is always perpendicular to v, so it does no work: R is also true. But R is not why the particle goes straight; a force that does no work can still bend the path (circular motion when v ⊥ B). The reason is that the force is zero.
steps: F = qvB sin θ with θ = 0° gives F = 0 → A is true
F ⊥ v always, so power F·v = 0 → R is true
R does not explain A: zero work does not mean zero deflection
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A is the trap: R is true, but zero work also holds when the particle moves in a circle, so it cannot explain the straight path.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The acceleration due to gravity at a depth R/2 below the Earth's surface is equal to the acceleration due to gravity at a height h above the surface. If R is the radius of the Earth, h is:

solution.concept: Variation of g with depth and with height
solution.explanation: Below the surface g falls linearly with depth; above it g falls as the inverse square of distance from the centre. Set the two equal.
steps: At depth d: g_d = g(1 − d/R) = g(1 − 1/2) = g/2
At height h: g_h = g / (1 + h/R)²
solution.why_others_wrong: R/4 comes from g_h ≈ g(1 − 2h/R), which is valid only when h ≪ R; here h is comparable to R. R/2 assumes depth and height act equally. √2 R forgets to subtract 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following molecules has a see-saw shape?

solution.concept: VSEPR theory: bond pairs and lone pairs around the central atom
solution.explanation: A see-saw shape comes from 4 bond pairs and 1 lone pair (5 electron pairs, trigonal bipyramidal arrangement with the lone pair in an equatorial position).
steps: SF₄: S has 6 valence electrons, 4 used in bonds → 4 bond pairs + 1 lone pair → see-saw
XeF₄: 4 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs → square planar
BF₃: 3 bond pairs, no lone pair → trigonal planar
CH₄: 4 bond pairs, no lone pair → tetrahedral

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A first-order reaction is 75% complete in 60 minutes. The time taken for it to be 50% complete is:

solution.concept: Half-life of a first-order reaction is independent of initial concentration
solution.explanation: 75% completion means 25% (one quarter) remains, which takes exactly two half-lives.
steps: 100% → 50% (one half-life) → 25% (two half-lives)
2 × t½ = 60 min
t½ = 30 min
solution.why_others_wrong: 45 min assumes the reaction proceeds at a constant rate (zero order).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For the cell Zn | Zn²⁺ (0.01 M) || Cu²⁺ (1 M) | Cu, E°cell = 1.10 V. The emf of the cell at 298 K is (take 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V):

solution.explanation: Cell reaction: Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, with n = 2. A lower product concentration (Zn²⁺) than reactant concentration (Cu²⁺) makes the emf larger than E°.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1.041 V gets the sign of the log term wrong. 1.218 V uses n = 1. 1.10 V ignores concentration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is square planar and diamagnetic.
Statement II: [NiCl₄]²⁻ is tetrahedral and paramagnetic.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Valence bond theory: strong- and weak-field ligands with a d⁸ ion
solution.explanation: Ni²⁺ is 3d⁸. CN⁻ is a strong-field ligand: it pairs the 3d electrons, leaving one 3d orbital free for dsp² hybridisation (square planar, no unpaired electrons). Cl⁻ is a weak-field ligand: no pairing, so sp³ hybridisation (tetrahedral) with two unpaired electrons.
steps: Ni²⁺: [Ar] 3d⁸
[Ni(CN)₄]²⁻: pairing → dsp² → square planar, 0 unpaired electrons → diamagnetic (Statement I true)
[NiCl₄]²⁻: no pairing → sp³ → tetrahedral, 2 unpaired electrons → paramagnetic (Statement II true)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', valence bond theory
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following compounds give a positive iodoform test?

(a) Ethanol
(b) Propan-2-ol
(c) Propan-1-ol
(d) Acetophenone
(e) Pentan-3-one

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The iodoform test is positive for compounds with a CH₃CO– group (methyl ketones and acetaldehyde), and for alcohols with a CH₃CH(OH)– group, which I₂/NaOH first oxidises to CH₃CO–.
steps: (a) Ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH → oxidised to CH₃CHO → positive
(b) Propan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ → oxidised to acetone → positive
(c) Propan-1-ol, CH₃CH₂CH₂OH → gives propanal, no CH₃CO– → negative
(d) Acetophenone, C₆H₅COCH₃ → methyl ketone → positive
(e) Pentan-3-one, CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH₃ → ethyl groups on both sides, no CH₃CO– → negative
solution.why_others_wrong: Pentan-3-one is the usual trap: it is a ketone but not a methyl ketone.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is absent in a typical bacterial cell?

solution.explanation: Bacteria have no membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria, plastids or a nucleus. They do have a plasma membrane, 70S ribosomes and (in most) a cell wall.
steps: Mitochondria are membrane-bound → absent in prokaryotes
Ribosomes (70S) are not membrane-bound → present
Plasma membrane and cell wall are parts of the bacterial cell envelope → present
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', prokaryotic cells

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (plant growth regulator) with List-II (effect).

List-I:
A. Auxin
B. Gibberellin
C. Cytokinin
D. Ethylene

List-II:
I. Promotes fruit ripening
II. Causes apical dominance
III. Delays leaf senescence
IV. Causes bolting in rosette plants

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Physiological effects of plant growth regulators
solution.explanation: Each regulator has a signature effect that NEET tests directly.
steps: Auxin: the growing apical bud inhibits lateral buds (apical dominance) → II
Gibberellin: internode elongation just before flowering in rosette plants such as cabbage (bolting) → IV
Cytokinin: promotes nutrient mobilisation and delays leaf senescence → III
Ethylene: enhances respiration rate during ripening (respiratory climacteric) → I
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a cross AaBbCc × AaBbCc, the three genes assort independently and each shows complete dominance. What fraction of the offspring will show the dominant phenotype for exactly one of the three traits?

solution.concept: Product rule for independently assorting genes
solution.explanation: For each gene, Aa × Aa gives the dominant phenotype with probability 3/4 and the recessive with 1/4. 'Exactly one dominant' can happen in 3 ways (which trait is dominant).
steps: P(dominant) = 3/4, P(recessive) = 1/4 for each trait
One particular arrangement, e.g. dominant–recessive–recessive: 3/4 × 1/4 × 1/4 = 3/64
Three such arrangements: 3 × 3/64 = 9/64
solution.why_others_wrong: 27/64 is the fraction for exactly two dominant traits (and also for all three). 3/64 counts only one arrangement. 1/64 is the triple-recessive fraction.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', dihybrid cross

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): C₄ plants show little or no photorespiration.
Reason (R): In C₄ plants the Calvin cycle runs in bundle sheath cells, where a high CO₂ concentration makes RuBisCO act mainly as a carboxylase.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: RuBisCO binds both CO₂ and O₂; photorespiration happens when it binds O₂. C₄ plants first fix CO₂ in mesophyll cells and release it in bundle sheath cells, raising the CO₂ concentration around RuBisCO. So RuBisCO's oxygenase activity is minimised. R is true and is exactly why A is true.
steps: Photorespiration = oxygenation of RuBP by RuBisCO
C₄ pathway concentrates CO₂ in bundle sheath cells
High CO₂ : O₂ ratio → carboxylation dominates → little photorespiration
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', photorespiration and the C₄ pathway
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Gross primary productivity minus the respiration losses of producers is the net primary productivity.
Statement II: Secondary productivity is the rate at which producers form new organic matter.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: GPP − R = NPP, so Statement I is true. Secondary productivity is the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers, not producers, so Statement II is false.
steps: NPP = GPP − R → Statement I true
Secondary productivity refers to consumers → Statement II false
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A person with blood group AB has:

options.text: No antigens on RBCs and both anti-A and anti-B antibodies in plasma
Antigens A and B on RBCs and no anti-A or anti-B antibodies in plasma
Antigens A and B on RBCs and both anti-A and anti-B antibodies in plasma
No antigens on RBCs and no antibodies in plasma

solution.explanation: The blood group is named after the antigens on the RBCs. The plasma carries antibodies only against the antigens the person lacks, so group AB has neither antibody. This is why AB people are called universal recipients.
steps: Group AB → antigens A and B on RBCs
Both antigens present → no anti-A, no anti-B in plasma
solution.why_others_wrong: The first option describes group O. Having both antigen and its antibody (third option) would make the person's own blood clump.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', ABO grouping
solution.final_answer: Option B: Antigens A and B on RBCs and no anti-A or anti-B antibodies in plasma

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about antidiuretic hormone (ADH) are correct?

(a) It is released into the blood from the neurohypophysis.
(b) It increases water reabsorption from the latter parts of the renal tubule.
(c) Its deficiency causes diabetes insipidus.
(d) It is secreted by the adrenal cortex.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: ADH (vasopressin) is made by hypothalamic neurons and released from the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis). It makes the distal tubule and collecting duct reabsorb more water. Too little ADH causes diabetes insipidus: large volumes of dilute urine.
steps: (a) True: stored in and released from the neurohypophysis
(b) True: acts on the distal parts of the tubule
(c) True: deficiency → diabetes insipidus
(d) False: the adrenal cortex secretes aldosterone, not ADH
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', regulation of kidney function

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, 16% of individuals show a recessive trait (genotype aa). Among the individuals who do NOT show the trait, what fraction are carriers (Aa)?

solution.explanation: q² is the recessive fraction; find q and p, then compare carriers (2pq) with all individuals showing the dominant trait (p² + 2pq).
steps: AA = p² = 0.36, Aa = 2pq = 0.48 → normal individuals = 0.84
Carriers among normal = 0.48 / 0.84 = 4/7 ≈ 0.57
solution.why_others_wrong: 12/25 (0.48) is the carrier fraction of the whole population, not of the normal individuals asked about. 3/7 is the AA share among normal individuals. 3/5 is p.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (disease) with List-II (causative organism).

List-I:
A. Typhoid
B. Malaria
C. Ascariasis
D. Ringworm

List-II:
I. Plasmodium vivax
II. Trichophyton
III. Salmonella typhi
IV. Ascaris lumbricoides

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Common human diseases and their pathogens
solution.explanation: Typhoid is bacterial, malaria is protozoan, ascariasis is caused by a roundworm (helminth) and ringworm by fungi.
steps: Typhoid → Salmonella typhi (bacterium) → III
Malaria → Plasmodium (protozoan) → I
Ascariasis → Ascaris (intestinal roundworm) → IV
Ringworm → fungi of genera Microsporum, Trichophyton, Epidermophyton → II
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Human Health and Disease', common diseases in humans
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The restriction endonuclease EcoRI cuts DNA at random sites.
Reason (R): EcoRI recognises the palindromic nucleotide sequence 5'-GAATTC-3'.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Restriction endonucleases cut only at specific recognition sequences. EcoRI recognises the palindrome GAATTC and cuts between G and A on each strand, leaving sticky ends. So A is false and R is true.
steps: Restriction endonucleases are sequence-specific → A is false
EcoRI site: 5'-GAATTC-3' / 3'-CTTAAG-5', a palindrome → R is true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', restriction enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.
